div.p: The Enterprise-Wide Risk Assessment (EWRA) constitutes a comprehensive evaluation framework designed to assess the organization's exposure to Money Laundering (ML), Terrorist Financing (TF), and Proliferation Financing (PF) risks across all operational business units and service lines.

The fundamental purpose of this methodology is to establish a data-driven, repeatable, and fully auditable framework that ensures strict adherence to Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations, Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS) industry standards, and applicable local regulatory requirements.

p.strong: The EWRA outcomes serve multiple critical organizational functions:

ul.li: Risk Identification and Quantification: Systematically identify and measure risk exposures across all material risk pillars
Control Enhancement and Resource Optimization: Inform strategic decisions regarding control framework improvements and optimal allocation of compliance resources
Governance and Oversight Support: Provide senior management and the Board of Directors with comprehensive, actionable intelligence

div.p: The EWRA framework systematically evaluates risk exposure through a comprehensive multi-dimensional analysis structure. Each risk pillar represents a distinct dimension of the organization's AML/CFT risk profile:

ul.li: Customer Risk (40% Weight) – Risk arising from customer relationships, characteristics, and CRA assessment results
Products & Services Risk (25% Weight) – Risk inherent in the institution's product and service offerings
Geography Risk (20% Weight) – Risk associated with jurisdictional exposure and geographic operations
Delivery Channel Risk (15% Weight) – Risk related to customer onboarding and service delivery methods
Supplier Risk (0% Weight) – Optional risk stemming from third-party relationships (currently not weighted)

div.p: Risk Rating Scale: 1 = Low Risk, 2 = Medium Risk, 3 = High Risk

The EWRA framework incorporates rigorous data quality controls to ensure assessment accuracy and reliability. All critical data elements utilized in risk scoring calculations are designated as mandatory fields. The platform enforces strict data completeness validation, preventing the persistence or export of any records that fail to satisfy completeness requirements.

p.strong: The following fields constitute mandatory data requirements:

ul.li: Customer classification (individual or corporate entity)
Residency jurisdiction and nationality information
Country of incorporation and Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) nationalities
Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status and sanctions screening results
Customer onboarding and service delivery channel
Associated product(s) and service(s) relationships

p.strong: This comprehensive data governance approach delivers:

ul.li: Complete Data Coverage: 100% data completeness across all EWRA assessment inputs
Computational Accuracy: Precise and consistent calculation of risk scores through verified data sets
Regulatory Defensibility: Comprehensive documentation and full audit traceability

div.p: The EWRA methodology employs a structured, three-stage sequential assessment process designed to ensure systematic and comprehensive risk evaluation:

ol.li: Inherent Risk Calculation – Automated system computation utilizing comprehensive customer and transaction data to establish baseline risk exposure levels prior to the application of mitigating controls

Control Effectiveness Assessment – User-directed evaluation of control framework strength, incorporating validated percentage inputs that reflect the actual effectiveness of implemented AML/CFT controls
Residual Risk Calculation – System-generated final risk determination based on pre-defined control logic, quantifying the remaining risk exposure after accounting for control effectiveness

div.p: Definition: Inherent Risk represents the level of ML/TF/PF exposure before applying mitigating controls.
System Logic: The system automatically calculates an inherent score per pillar using embedded field logic. Each pillar's score is derived as a weighted mean:

p.style: margin-bottom: 0.5rem; color: #4b5563; font-family: monospace; background: #f3f4f6; padding: 0.5rem; border-radius: 4px;

div.p: (1 × Low% + 2 × Medium% + 3 × High%) ÷ 100
Risk level thresholds are configurable via EWRA Settings. Default thresholds: 1.0 to < 1.7 = Low, 1.7 to < 2.4 = Medium, 2.4 to 3.0 = High
Definition: Control Effectiveness measures the strength of AML/CFT controls mitigating inherent risk.
Input and Calculation: Users select control effectiveness per pillar or enter a justified custom percentage.

p.strong: Alternatively, users may apply the Control Library:

ul.li: EDD – 15%
SOW – 10%
SOF – 10%
Adverse Media – 12%
UBO Verification – 15%
Site Visit – 20%

div.p: Rules: Total control percentage capped at 70%. Minimum 35% required to qualify for a one-level downgrade in risk.
Definition: Residual Risk = Remaining exposure after applying control effectiveness.

ul.li: Confirmed Sanctions = Decline / Block
Foreign or Senior PEP = Minimum High Residual

div.p: Definition: The Final Risk Rank represents the organization's consolidated AML/CFT exposure after controls.
Calculation: Final Risk Rank = Weighted Average of All Pillar Residual Risks

Products & Services – 25%
Geography – 20%
Delivery Channel – 15%

ul.li: Low + Medium + High = 100% ± 0.1
Control total ≤ 70% cap
Downgrade limited to one level only
All mandatory fields completed – no missing data
PEP and Sanctions overrides enforced consistently

div.p: The EWRA platform incorporates sophisticated automated reporting capabilities that transform quantitative risk assessments into comprehensive, executive-ready documentation.

ul.li: Per-Pillar Risk Metrics: Detailed outputs for each risk pillar showing Inherent Risk, Control Effectiveness, and Residual Risk
Visual Risk Heatmap: Color-coded graphical representation of Residual Risk across all pillars
Consolidated Assessment Table: Comprehensive tabular summary displaying all key metrics in audit-ready format
Final Risk Rank Summary: Organization-wide risk assessment presented in both numeric and qualitative formats

p.strong: The integrated AI narrative engine produces:

ul.li: Executive Summary (120–160 words): High-level synthesis for senior management and board audiences
Per-Pillar Analysis (80–120 words each): Detailed risk commentary explaining drivers and control effectiveness
Conclusion (60–100 words): Forward-looking summary addressing recommended actions

div.p: The EWRA framework operates within a robust governance structure that ensures appropriate oversight, accountability, and regulatory compliance.

ul.li: Assessment Frequency: Annual basis as minimum, with additional assessments triggered by material changes
Multi-Level Review: Rigorous review by Compliance, approval by Senior Management, endorsement by Board of Directors
Settings Documentation: Automatic snapshot of all system configurations preserved for audit purposes
Historical Archive: All assessment results systematically archived with full version control

div.p: The EWRA framework incorporates a systematic continuous improvement process that leverages assessment outcomes to drive enhancements in the organization's AML/CFT risk management capabilities.

ul.li: Control Framework Enhancement: Identification of control gaps and opportunities for strengthening mitigation measures
Risk Parameter Calibration: Systematic refinement of risk classification methodologies
Threshold Optimization: Ongoing adjustment of risk thresholds and control effectiveness weightings
Methodology Validation: Continuous validation of system accuracy and alignment with regulatory standards
